@dgroup @llorllale there are two things in the todo:
1. Some matchers in cactoos-matchers makes the method `matchesSafely` public, and when testing the matcher, those methods are tested. This is incorrect: to test the matcher and ensure they work properly, they must be tested directly as an argument of `assertThat` as in [ScalarHasValueTest#L54](https://github.com/llorllale/cactoos-matchers/blob/master/src/test/java/org/llorllale/cactoos/matchers/ScalarHasValueTest.java#L54).
The test for [EndsWithTest](https://github.com/llorllale/cactoos-matchers/blob/master/src/test/java/org/llorllale/cactoos/matchers/EndsWithTest.java) is not correct because it tests the method `matchesSafely` directly instead of testing the real behaviour of the matcher (the one normally invoked by `assertThat` and that is partially implemented by the superclasses `TypeSafeMatcher` and `BaseMatcher`) (btw, this is why inheritance is hell to test sometimes ;).
2. The matchers should report failure to match properly. Implementing `describeMismatchSafely` is the mean to do that when subclassing `TypeSafeMatcher`. You can see how this can then be tested correctly in [ScalarHasValueTest#L87](https://github.com/llorllale/cactoos-matchers/blob/master/src/test/java/org/llorllale/cactoos/matchers/ScalarHasValueTest.java#L87). I am not clear what `TypeSafeDiagnosingMatcher` is for, but if it allows for matcher to properly describe the mismatch, then I think it's ok to use it.
